title: TuneScope
tagline: A standalone ESP32-S3 music recognition device with a real-time OLED audio visualizer.
problem: I wanted to explore whether a standalone embedded device could identify songs without relying on a smartphone. The goal was to build a dedicated music recognition device that records nearby audio, sends it to an online recognition service over Wi-Fi, and presents the results through a polished OLED interface while maintaining a clean, modular firmware architecture.

components.name: ESP32-S3 N16R8
components.purpose: Main controller responsible for audio capture, networking, processing, and display.

components.name: INMP441 I2S Microphone
components.purpose: Captures nearby music as digital PCM audio.

components.name: SSD1306 128×64 OLED
components.purpose: Displays recognition status, song information, and the real-time audio visualizer.

components.name: Push Button
components.purpose: Recognition trigger and display mode switching.

timeline.title: Hardware Bring-up
timeline.desc: Initialized the ESP32-S3, OLED, microphone, Wi-Fi, and verified PSRAM functionality.

timeline.title: Audio Processing
timeline.desc: Implemented continuous audio capture, RMS calculation, and a real-time OLED audio visualizer.

timeline.title: Recording Pipeline
timeline.desc: Built a PSRAM-based recorder and generated valid WAV files from raw PCM audio.

timeline.title: Cloud Recognition
timeline.desc: Integrated the AudD Music Recognition API using HTTPS, multipart uploads, and JSON parsing.

timeline.title: User Interface
timeline.desc: Designed a modular OLED interface featuring splash screens, status pages, title scrolling, and multiple display modes.

timeline.title: Optimization & Documentation
timeline.desc: Optimized rendering performance, improved architecture, documented the project, and prepared it for public release.

failures: Incorrect I2S configuration initially produced invalid microphone data.
OLED flickering caused by excessive full-screen redraws.
Managing large audio buffers required migrating recording to PSRAM.
Constructing multipart/form-data requests for HTTPS uploads was more complex than expected.
Recognition and UI logic became tightly coupled before introducing a dedicated DisplayManager.
Long song titles exceeded the OLED width and required an automatic scrolling system.

reflections.what_worked: Breaking the project into independent modules greatly simplified debugging and made the firmware easier to extend. Separating rendering from business logic through a DisplayManager significantly improved maintainability.
reflections.what_failed: Early versions mixed hardware control, networking, and display updates together, making debugging difficult. Some performance issues also stemmed from unnecessary OLED redraws before optimizing the rendering pipeline.
reflections.next_time: I would design an event-driven architecture from the beginning, add automated testing for individual modules, and implement OTA updates and local audio analysis to reduce reliance on cloud recognition.
